segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: If you have ever scaled your Facebook Ads and then watched your ROAS tank as soon as you push that budget up,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: and then as a result you have to scale back down and you continue to bash your head against the wall trying to figure out how can I actually scale Meta without it completely tanking on me.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Well, in this week's video, I'm going to show you the exact scaling process that we use to scale brands to spending over $100,000 a day on ads

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: and show you the different levels of where you should be focusing and how you should be scaling based off of your current daily spend.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: I'm also going to shatter your beliefs of what you actually think is possible when it comes to media buying on Meta by showing you some seriously big numbers.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Here's an actual screenshot of a brand spending $50,000 on a single campaign.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And most importantly, I'm going to give you the exact process and SOP that our team uses to scale ad accounts every single day

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: and help our brands and our community of 300+ Shopify brand owners in Evolve scale towards 100k days.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Now, I'll be honest, there is absolutely nothing in the world that gives me more dopamine or fires me up more

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: than being able to go into Meta, click on the budget tab, and increase that budget and, sometimes, even double it.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: So I am absolutely pumped to bring you this week's video.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: If you've been wanting to scale your Facebook Ads and again you don't have a strategy in doing so, this video is 100% for you.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Let's go ahead and jump in.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: All right. So, as you see on screen here, there are going to be specific levels that we go through in this video based on where your current daily spend is.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Now, before we actually unlock the certain levels and the actual structural and tactical things that you will be doing in the ad account at each level in front of you,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: we first need to understand how to actually scale. Okay?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And so, how we actually scale is down here in the EAM scaling process, and this applies to the campaigns that are in your account and what you currently have an active budget on.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Now, I am going to go through this pretty quickly, but again, this process is pretty straightforward and you can go back in the video if you want to re-watch.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Again, I will stop and emphasize the points that need to be emphasized. But for the most part, step one is pretty simple: is this campaign hitting target KPI?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And to add a caveat to that, I would add that is your entire ad account actually hitting target KPI,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: because as we scroll up here into the specific levels, there are going to be some specific things that we add at each stage. So again, make sure you keep watching the video to see those next levels.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: But with that said, the first question is, are we hitting target KPI?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Now, if the answer is yes, we're actually going to go down the yes train first, you need to ask yourself if you are in scaling protocol.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Now, you might be wondering, what the heck is scaling protocol?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Well, scaling protocol is essentially where you scale the ad account every 24 hours. Okay?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: If you are not in scaling protocol, you are going to go down the no train, and I'm actually going to explain what scaling protocol is. Again, it's not that hard to understand.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Or, you'll see here, if you are looking at a limited-time promo or sale campaign—say, for example, you're running a Fourth of July campaign, or you're running a Black Friday campaign, and that has a hard end date—

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: then you are able to actually go straight into scaling protocol, and you do not have to wait.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: So assuming you're not running a promo or sale campaign, and that you're just going to say no to this, "I'm just running my regular campaign."

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And again, if you don't know what a promo or sale campaign is, I am going to show you guys an ad account that we scaled to $100,000 a day with the promo structure. So again, we're going to tap into that.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: But again, if you said no here, you can scroll down and you can see that we have updated this to say, "Has there been 48 to 72 hours of performance consistently above target KPI?"

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Now, if you're wondering what scaling protocol is, this is what scaling protocol is. Okay?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: If you have seen two to three days of consistent performance above your target KPI, you are officially in scaling protocol, which means that you can start scaling your ad account every 24 hours.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: So for example, on Monday, if you check and you're at a 3x ROAS, and that is above your KPI, that would be the first 24 hours. Okay?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: So when you come down here and you see, "Has there been 48 to 72 hours of consistent performance?" You would say no.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And then what you would do is you would just wait another 24 hours.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: So let's say Tuesday, we come back and again we see that there has now been another day at a 3x ROAS, and you have now had 48 hours of consistent target KPI performance.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Then, you can say yes and go down the train of checking whether or not it is click-based data.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Now, I'm going to come back to this, because the final thing that I wanted to mention here is recently we've added a new step to this, which says, "Is there a new reason to be scaling?"

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And what we mean by that is have you essentially found a new winning ad, have you found a new winning offer, or have you found a new winning landing page, or has something happened inside

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: of the ad account that is leading to dramatically better performance within that period? Because there have been times when we go through where we see this question and we are not in Scaling Protocol,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: and we are not running a limited time promo campaign, but we have just launched a new winning ad and the thing is taking off like a rocket ship,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: and it's taken our ROAS from a 2x to a 5x. Because in case you didn't know, winning ads and winning offers and winning landing pages can actually do that for your ad account.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Then there will be times where we will say, "Yes, there is a new reason to be scaling." And again, we will confirm now whether or not it is all click-based data.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And for those of you that don't know what click-based data is, essentially when you go into your ad account—so, for example, here is an ad account here that I'm actually going to pull up when it comes to the scaling levels.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: So again, just a reminder, if you want to actually see the levels of scale over here, you've got to keep on watching. But to see how much of your data is actually click-based,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: what you're going to do is you're going to click on "Columns", you're going to click "Compare attribution settings", and you're going to take a look at your seven-day click-based data. And now this is assuming that you are going to be running

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: seven-day click, one-day view. So again, for the sake of this brand, that is what they're running. It says multiple attribution, but let me just go and show you the active ad sets.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: So, as you can see, this brand is running seven-day click, one-day view. And actually on this Champions ad set, we're running or one-day engaged-view. Now this is a whole another topic. Just know it doesn't really matter.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: You're just going to scroll over to make sure that all of the data or most of the data is actually click-based.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: So, as you can see here, there are 111 purchases, and out of those purchases, 104 are click-based. And so if we scroll to our click-based ROAS, you can see we're at a 2.4.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Now again, the reason that we do this is because we want to see that the ads are actually driving the performance and it's not just collecting a bunch of view-through attribution.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Now I have gone back and forth on view-through attribution and I do think there is a place for it. However, when it comes to incrementality and essentially like whatever provides an incremental lift

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: and what is going to drive the sales that you see on your actual store, I prefer to look at click-based data.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And so this is where we look to see if 60% or more of the purchases are click-based or click-based data is actually meeting KPI, then you can go ahead and scale.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Okay? And so in this instance, when it comes to the actual buttons, because we've made it this far now, we are either going to increase the budget by 20% flat, okay?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: So again, if you're spending $100 a day, you would increase it by 20%, which puts you to 120.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Now if you have very big budgets and say you're spending $10,000 a day or $100,000 a day, obviously a 20% budget increase is quite a lot, right?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: That goes up to $2,000 additional and up to $20,000 if you're actually spending $100,000 a day. So unless you're at those budgets, again, you can scale by 20%.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Now if you are at those budgets, we have at times scaled by 15% or 10% or 5%, but it really does depend on the brand. For most people, you can actually scale 20%.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: If you notice that you have over-scaled, and again, when you come back to check and you're not hitting target KPI, then you can of course scale down. And again, we're going to talk about the process for that as well.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: But as you can see here, on the other side, if you are at 50 to 100% above KPI—so say your target is a 2x and you are actually getting a 4x return on ad spend—

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: there are times where we will double or 1.5x the actual budget. So again, as another example down here, if your target is 2.5 and performance is at 3.75,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: aka 50% above your target, and just as a reminder, that is actually happening consistently and it's not just one day,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: well, then what you can do is you can actually increase your budget by however much you are above. Just know, do this at your own risk. And if you are dealing with bigger budgets,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: obviously, chad scaling from 10k a day to 20k per day is a massive jump, right? But if you're spending $200 a day, $200 to $400 a day

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: not really that big of a difference. Okay?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: So just understand that as you play with bigger numbers, you are going to want to be less aggressive.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: But if you are less than a thousand dollars a day or even less than two or three thousand dollars a day, you're probably fine to be more aggressive with how you scale.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Just again make sure you see where your KPI is at.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Now, if we climb back up here, I just want to emphasize this again.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: If there is a new reason to be scaling, you can scale within 24 hours.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: But we still, a lot of the times, even if we hit a new winning ad or a new winning offer, we will wait 48 hours just to see how it's doing,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: or we'll wait like 36 hours. So we'll let it run for a day, and then if we check it the next day and it's still crushing or off to a really good start, then sometimes we will scale.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: But I just want to clarify that.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And then again, if you are not in scaling protocol, there's no new reason to be scaling, wait another 24 hours.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And same thing here, if more than 60% of purchases are not click-based, so basically a lot of view-through data is coming in, wait another 24 hours.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And at this point, I would actually check and potentially switch to seven-day click-only, but that's a topic for another video.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Now, let's go down the no train here. Okay?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: So if you are not hitting target KPI, then the first question that you need to ask yourself is, are you below breakeven KPI for 24 to 48 hours?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Now, this is a question that we recently added, because we have seen some people ultimately Chad-scale and just tank their account.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And for a lot of you guys, you'll scale up and then all of a sudden your ROAS just tanks.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And so, you want to give Meta time to figure itself out, because when you increase budget, it has to expand its reach and it has to serve your ads to more people.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And what ends up happening and the reason why your ads can't scale when you do this majority of the time is because the creatives are just not good enough, right?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: So you have creatives that are able to, say, reach, you know, 10,000 people a day and get them to convert.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: But as soon as you try to scale beyond those 10,000 people, Meta is now having to show your ads to colder and colder people.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And because your ads are not good enough to convert those colder and colder people, you see your return on ad spend tank, right?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And spend becomes really inefficient.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: So if you are below breakeven KPI for whatever reason, so after 24 or 48 hours,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: what we would recommend doing is checking if you're at minimum daily spend, and again minimum daily spend I'm going to come back to in a second, but then likely just scale down and decrease the budget 20%. Okay?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: The minimum that we usually scale is around 20%.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: It's very, very rare that we'll scale down like 10%.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And there are times where we will scale down more aggressively. It really depends on the scenario.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And again, we're going to get more into that.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: But if for whatever reason you're not at breakeven or you're not below breakeven, but you are not really hitting your KPI,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: so again, for example, if your target is a 2.5 and you're at a 2,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: obviously you're not losing money, but it's not your ideal target. So in that instance,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: what you can ask yourself is again, has there been 48 to 72 hours of

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: performance consistently below your target?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And again, we're emphasizing this on a seven-day click-based data.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: So if you have seen two to three days of poor performance, then what we would recommend doing

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: is, again, checking if you're at minimum spend, but if you're not, again wait 24 hours. Very, very simple.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: But if you are, then check if you're at minimum daily spend and likely, again, decrease your budget down.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Now, what is minimum daily spend?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Well, minimum daily spend is essentially how much you're willing to spend no matter what. Okay?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And this changes as you get bigger as a brand. Okay? Because you'll likely have more cash.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: For a lot of you guys, when you're just starting out, you're probably maybe spending $50 to $100 a day.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And so that is likely your minimum daily spend, where no matter what, that is what you're going to spend for 30 days.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Now, for some of our brands, because we're spending a lot more, say we're spending 10, 15, 20, or 30k a day,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: our minimum spend for a brand spending 20k a day might be 10, meaning that no matter what, like, we're spending 10k a day and we better figure it out, right?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And so calculating your minimum daily spend is more of an exercise that you can do based off of the cash flow and the reserves that you have.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: But for most of you guys, I would say like your minimum daily spend should be like $100 or $200 a day, and if you continue to go down, down, down, down, down,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: well, then you're going to have to really figure some things out here, which is why we have this updated area down here.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Okay, so whether or not you're decreasing budget or you are at your minimum daily spend and you can't decrease anymore,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: it's very, very, very important for you to actually take action outside of the ad account. Okay?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And I cannot stress this enough, because if you are scaling down, you need to focus on the things that actually allow you to scale. Okay?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Which is, number one, launching new DCTs. Okay?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Number two, double-checking the funnel for bugs or errors.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: You wouldn't believe how many times that we've seen brands break something on their website.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: We check the ad account the next day, performance is totally tanked,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: and now we're trying to figure out what's going on. But because we have a process for double-checking the entire funnel,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: what we actually do is we go and check the website and boom, all of a sudden we found that the client accidentally removed a piece of code for their cart or changed something on the product page

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: or they're out of stock. Okay?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And so it's very, very important to make sure that your media buyers specifically or you specifically have a process for double-checking your funnel

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: if you see performance going down. Okay?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: This is actually something that I'd recommend doing every day, especially if you see a dramatic change in the funnel. Most of you guys do this automatically because you just

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: spam your ad account and spam your Shopify, but for the most part, make sure you double-check your funnel.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Now, the other thing that you should be doing is conducting data analysis on ads that are getting spend, and processing learnings and completing feedback loops to understand,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: okay, Meta is liking this angle or Meta is liking this avatar or Meta is liking this style of creative,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: what can I learn from it? How can I make better ads?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And make sure that you complete those feedback loops so you're not wasting your time when you go to create new DCTs, because again,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: you need to learn from what is happening in the account. And if you're new to the channel, I have tons of videos that talk about that.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And I actually just made a video about processing learnings, so you can actually go and check that out. I'll make sure the team leaves a link in the description down below.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: But from there, you can also conduct deep research for new avatars and new mechanisms.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And this is something that I really want to double-click into, because I think some of you guys start to panic when Meta is tanking,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: and you're constantly looking in the ad account for answers. But the truth is,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: the reason why your ad account is tanking is because what's actually inside of it. And this is where it's so confusing

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: because you see that the inside of the ad account is tanking, and so you want to try to fix the inside of the ad account,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: a.k.a you want to fix the campaigns and the structure and all that kind of stuff.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: But what is actually going to fix the inside of your ad account is everything outside.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And so if you are seeing that performance is going down and that every time you scale you get hit and punched in the face,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: well, it's probably time for you to spend more time outside of the ad account,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: focusing on deep research, finding new mechanisms and new ways to position your product,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: finding new avatars and people with specific pain points that you can go after,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: and finding new creatives and studying existing creatives or even looking at creatives. And this is what I love so much about Evolve,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: because the first thing that we show people when they join Evolve is a winning ads document of ads that have spent

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: millions of dollars, and so they right away are able to adjust their lens of what a good ad looks like, so they can go and create them.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: So, if you're struggling in your ad account, you need to understand what a great ad is,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: and then from there, you need to put in the work again outside of the ad account to actually get the inside of the ad account to start working better.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Wanted to go full screen just to make sure I emphasized that.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And then from there, the final thing that you can do, and this is something that we again started doing recently and it's so so important for you to understand, is to start offer testing, okay?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: If you are a brand that has been plateaued for a few months and you haven't been able to scale, or maybe you're scaling back down, or even then you're at your minimum daily budget,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: you should likely start testing some new offers, right?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: The market is going to get sophisticated.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: The offer that you ran in January is probably not as powerful as it is now in June.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And on top of that, desires are shifting. Desires are changing.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Unless you live in the Arctic, it's also summer right now.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: So, again, when I say desires are shifting and changing, people have different buying habits. People are outside more. People are traveling more.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: You need to figure out how you can create offers that are going to appeal to those specific types of people,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: and you also need to understand how to make offers that can scale through specific seasons and specific periods where everything might not be in your favor, okay?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And so, my favorite way to do offer testing is, again, to do it inside of your one campaign and test brand new ads with a brand new offer in that campaign to see if it gets spent.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Now, if you are a brand that is a little bit more scaled, maybe you're spending 10 to 15k per day, you likely have enough data to go and split test it formerly on your store.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: But with that said, I still love just creating new offers, focusing on the avatar, which again, why deep research is so important, and coming up with different pricing strategies, different bundles,

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: and all of that good stuff, actually be able to test it inside of your ad account and see if that can give you the lightning bolt that you need to get you out of your minimum daily spend or to get you off of this plateau or decreased budget protocol that you are in.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: So, that is the entire scaling SOP up to date with exactly what we do.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Now, if you hung in there to the end, you're going to get the sauce over here of something that we've recently just put together that is our levels of scaling, okay?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And so, level one of scaling is 0 to 50k per day.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Now, I know this sounds ridiculous and this sounds super weird, like how can my scaling setup be the same at $0 to 50k?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Well, it's because that's where Meta is pushing everything and there's proof of it.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: So, again, if you are a brand that is spending $100 per day, this is what your ad account should look like, and again, you should apply scaling protocol to this campaign.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: As you can see here, $360 a day budget, if we are hitting KPI, we are going to scale. It's very, very simple, okay?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: So, you just follow everything that we went through for that one campaign.

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: Now, for those of you that are wondering, "Well, why 50k per day?", right? "How come this one campaign is spending 360?"

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: And as I'm about to show you, here's an actual screenshot of a brand spending $50,000 on a single campaign, okay?

segments.speaker: Presenter
segments.text: How is that possible? It's because it's all about the things that are outside of your ad account, okay?

segments.speaker: Presenter
